Repo: Tendril (current directory). Contest: per-occurrence edits of repeating things. Main files: shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/tendril/app/data/habit/HabitScheduleEdit.kt, HabitBlock.kt, domain CalendarSchedule.kt (EditScope), PlanCodec, data/entry/Entry.kt (originalEntryId, originalOccurrenceDate, isExceptionSkip), EntryDao.kt (exceptions), the use cases that edit one occurrence of a task/event and of a calendar habit, and the sync orchestrator.
Claims (verify each; quote the rule):
1. HabitScheduleEdit columns: list every column with type. target is HABIT or BLOCK; scope and changes are opaque encoded strings.
2. EditScope cases are Occurrence, Day, Week, From and Extra; say exactly what each one means (one occurrence, every habit on a day, a whole week, this and following, an added occurrence) and how its changes are applied (in insertion order? latest wins?).
3. A 'From' (this and following) edit on a habit is stored as an edit row, not by splitting the series into two habits; for a task/event, say how 'this and following' is done (split the Entry? not supported?).
4. Task/event exceptions are Entry rows: a skip row (isExceptionSkip) or an override row with recurrenceRule = null; list what an override may change (time, date, title, duration).
5. The planner's weekly placements (TimesPerWeek) are stored as HabitScheduleEdit rows (Extra or Occurrence), or recomputed and not stored; quote.
6. HabitBlock.overrides (per-weekday times, e.g. SAT,SUN@480-630) is a standing rule, and a one-day block change is a HabitScheduleEdit with target BLOCK.
7. Sync: HabitScheduleEdit is inserted once and tombstoned once; Entry exception rows merge last-writer-wins; two devices editing the same occurrence differently: which wins in each mechanism.

Repo: Chronicle (current directory). Contest: per-occurrence edits of repeating things. Main files: the reminder domain (RepeatRule, RepeatSchedule), ReminderEntity, the reminder edit screen and any skip/snooze/postpone action.
Claims (verify each; quote the rule; report zero hits with the pattern if absent):
1. A repeating reminder can skip one occurrence without changing the rule; say how it is stored (a field on the reminder? a separate row?).
2. A repeating reminder can move or retime one occurrence only; say how it is stored.
3. 'This and following' edits exist; say how.
4. Snooze of one occurrence is stored on the reminder row (which column) and cleared at the next occurrence.

Repo: Mnemo (current directory). Contest: per-occurrence edits of repeating things. Main files: app/src/main/kotlin/com/hazia/mnemo/ (Reminder, ScheduleType, ScheduleCalculator, the edit screen, snooze).
Claims (verify each; quote the rule; report zero hits with the pattern if absent):
1. A repeating (CRON or STOCHASTIC) reminder can skip one occurrence without changing the rule; say how it is stored.
2. One occurrence can be moved or retimed; say how.
3. Snooze of one occurrence is stored on the reminder (which column) and what happens to the next occurrence.
